issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the exercise materials disagree about the collection type to use for the Farm's animals. In the UML in problem_statement.md the attribute is declared as List<Animal> (problem_statement.md line 17). In the textual instructions the Farm is described as requiring uniqueness and explicitly says the aggregation should be realized using a Set implemented with a HashSet (problem_statement.md lines 108-111). The provided solution implementation declares the field as private List<Animal> animals (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 9). This mismatch (List vs Set/HashSet) affects whether students must enforce uniqueness and which collection type and getter/setter signatures to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Farm.animals collection type consistent across artifacts. Preferred resolution: follow the textual instruction and use Set<Animal> (backed by a HashSet) to enforce uniqueness. Update the UML in problem_statement.md to show Set<Animal> and change the solution and template Farm.java to declare 'private Set<Animal> animals', initialize it with 'new HashSet<>()' in the no-arg constructor, and update getter/setter signatures and imports. Alternatively, if a List is intended, revise the textual instructions to remove the Set/HashSet requirement and state List<Animal> instead. Apply the chosen change uniformly to problem_statement.md, the template, and the solution to avoid student confusion.
